historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case 10-year revenue CAGR from the explicit ounces x mid-cycle price build (FY26 7,623 -> FY36 ~11,280); no historical CAGR is used as a driver because every one of them is dominated by the gold-price cycle and the FY21 Saracen and FY25 De Grey scrip mergers
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR 14.5% vs EPS 5-yr CAGR 0.3%: equity grew through scrip issuance (Saracen FY21 ~A$5.8bn, De Grey FY25 ~A$5bn) rather than retained earnings, and FY21 EPS of A$1.147 carried a one-off Saracen gain. 3-yr EPS CAGR of 31.9% is gold-price driven (realised A$2,750 -> A$4,925/oz).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC - IFRS-16 lease principal (treatment B): FY21 289.8, FY23 124.1, FY26 159.4. The owner-FCF 5-yr CAGR (-11.3%) is far below reported FCF (+4.2%): the gap is lease-financed fleet growth (principal 80.9 -> 273.2) and SBC (13 -> 38), i.e. an increasing share of reported cash generation is being spent through financing lines. Both series are also depressed by growth capex rather than by operating decline (cash earnings A$2.9bn FY26).

scenario_narratives.base: Gold-price mean reversion to A$4,400/oz by FY30 (still ~60% above the FY21-25 average) combined with a haircut version of the growth plan: KCGM to ~900koz on the 27Mtpa mill by FY29-30, Hemi first gold FY30, group ~2.4Moz by FY34. FY27 is a transition year inside guidance (1,560koz at AISC ~A$3,250) with realised prices near the H2 FY26 exit rate. Mid-cycle EBITDA margin 44-45%, capex intensity 18% once KCGM/Hemi are built. Terminal value capped at 12x owner FCF (cyclical).
scenario_narratives.bull: Gold plateaus at A$5,200-5,700/oz, the company delivers 2.5Mozpa by FY29-31 with KCGM unit costs falling on scale, margins hold at FY25-26 levels (~55-58%), and the board refresh improves capital allocation. This is roughly what the current price requires.
scenario_narratives.bear: Gold retraces to A$3,600/oz, KCGM ramps slowly, Hemi is deferred, output plateaus ~2.0Moz and above-peer unit costs leave a 33-35% EBITDA margin; owner FCF is thin through the decade. The bear does not hit the zero floor but is close to a cash-breakeven business in FY27-28 while growth capital is still being spent.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A gold producer is valued here on mid-cycle owner FCF, not on the FY26 peak-price year or on spot: revenue is an explicit ounces x realised AUD price build, EBITDA is revenue less an AISC-derived cash cost per ounce, IFRS-16 fleet leases are charged as an operating cost, SBC is expensed with the share count flat, growth capex for KCGM and Hemi is run through the explicit years and the terminal value is capped at 12x owner FCF. Cyclicality, execution and governance risk are charged once, in the scenario flows and a 30% bear weight, not in the discount rate. The gap between the weighted value and the market price is the price the market is paying for spot gold persisting plus full delivery of the 2.5Moz plan.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle gold price: every A$500/oz on the FY30+ realised price is worth roughly A$3-4/share in the base case; the model's A$4,400 is ~35% below the Sep-2026 spot-equivalent
KCGM 27Mtpa ramp (FY27-29) and Hemi FID/first gold (late FY27 / FY30): the ounce path is the second-largest driver and the company missed its previous volume target
Unit cost inflation: FY27 guided AISC A$3,050-3,450/oz is +20% on FY26; the base assumes unit costs improve with scale before inflating, which has not yet been demonstrated
AUD/USD: the realised AUD price embeds the currency multiplier; a stronger AUD cuts revenue with no offset in the AUD cost base
Governance: CEO transition (5-Oct-2026) and the Elliott board campaign could change capital allocation, force asset sales or delay Hemi
Terminal multiple: at a 12x cap the terminal value is ~55% of base EV; a 15x cap adds ~A$2/share

inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report cash flow reconciliation, 'Share-based payments' 38.0 (FY25: 27.6), NST.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt:8779; no separate equity-award tax withholding line disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes = 0)
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,424.7m ordinary shares on issue at the 10-Sep-2026 final-dividend record date (A$427.4m aggregate / 30.0c, FY26 AR note 16) plus 10.26m dilutive performance rights from the FY26 diluted-EPS denominator (note 20(d)) = 1,435.0m fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so grant dilution is already charged; the A$500m on-market buyback (A$129m executed by 30-Jun-2026, A$371m remaining) is the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat and is value-neutral here. No non-SBC issuance expected (the De Grey scrip issue of ~240m shares completed May 2025 and is already in the count).
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-built: Australian 10-year government bond ~4.3% + 5.5% equity risk premium x ~0.9 beta gives a ~9.3% cost of equity; ~5% pre-tax (3.5% after tax) on the US$600m 2033 notes and equipment finance at ~8% of capital gives ~9.0% WACC. No commodity, execution or governance premium is stacked on top: gold-price cyclicality, the KCGM/Hemi ramp risk, the CEO transition and the Elliott campaign are charged once, in the scenario flows and a 30% bear weight (adaptations section f).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Mining-fleet finance leases: A$273.2m principal (financing, AR:8620 area) plus ~A$20m lease interest inside the A$92.8m interest paid = ~A$293m FY26, 3.8% of revenue, charged via lease_cost_pct_path (3.8% easing to 3.0% as the fleet is increasingly bought outright). Lease liabilities (A$105.0m current + A$224.4m non-current = A$329.4m) are therefore EXCLUDED from total_debt; total_debt is borrowings only (A$208.8m + A$1,186.5m). da_pct_path is D&A ex right-of-use depreciation (~A$1,345m of the A$1,595.6m reported, ~17.6% of FY26 revenue) so the lease is not charged twice in cash-tax EBIT.
inputs.nci_treatment: None: no material non-controlling interest (100%-owned operations; the KCGM power-station JV is equity-accounted at A$16m).
inputs.net_debt_note: Cash and equivalents A$1,018.1m at 30-Jun-2026. The company's headline 'cash and bullion' A$1,235m adds A$217.2m of bullion awaiting settlement, which sits in trade receivables and is treated here as working capital, not cash (a ~A$0.15/share difference). Borrowings A$1,395.3m = US$600m 2033 senior notes plus USD equipment finance; the A$1.75bn corporate facilities were undrawn. Net debt A$377.2m. Net debt is positive, so interest income (A$47.5m) is NOT stripped from the FCF base. Rehabilitation provisions (A$883.9m non-current) are a real long-dated cash cost not separately deducted; they are absorbed in the mid-cycle capex intensity.
inputs.mid_cycle_note: FY26 is a peak-price year (realised A$4,925/oz vs a FY22-26 average of ~A$3,450 and a 10-year average of ~A$2,700) and management calls FY26 'peak investment' and FY27 a 'transition year'. Revenue is therefore NOT extrapolated from FY26: each scenario is an explicit ounces x realised-AUD-gold-price build, and EBITDA is revenue less an AISC-derived cash cost per ounce (FY26 EBITDA-level cost A$2,172/oz = AISC 2,698 less ~A$540m sustaining capex and A$273m lease payments; FY27 guided AISC mid A$3,250 less A$882m sustaining and ~A$290m leases = ~A$2,500/oz). Base mid-cycle price A$4,400/oz from FY30 (~US$3,080 at 0.70, in line with long-run sell-side gold decks and ~35% below the Sep-2026 spot-equivalent of ~A$6,800) with 2%/yr nominal drift from FY33; bear A$3,600 (near the FY25 realised level); bull A$5,200 (still below spot). FY27 realised prices (5,500 / 5,900 / 4,800) reflect the H2 FY26 exit rate of ~A$5,150 and ~20% of sales hedged at lower prices.
inputs.notes: Model: mid-cycle owner-FCF DCF, component route (owner_fcf_dcf_component), the same treatment as FMG.AX and CMM.AX. Routed as 'operating company, cyclical' via dcf-methods SKILL.md; owner-fcf.md and owner-fcf-adaptations.md read (currency-matched WACC, one lease treatment, risk charged once). Owner FCF FY0 = reported FCF 470.6 - SBC 38.0 - lease principal 273.2 = 159.4 (lease interest is already inside operating cash flow); this is the treatment-(B) owner-FCF anchor and is depressed by A$1.5-1.9bn of growth capital (KCGM Mill Expansion, Hemi, Fimiston South cutback) - the FY26 owner-FCF margin of 2.1% is NOT carried forward; the component build does that job. Ounce paths: base haircuts the company plan (2.5Mozpa by FY29) to ~2.4Moz by FY34 given the missed 2Moz FY26 target; bull delivers the plan; bear has KCGM ramping slowly and Hemi deferred to a ~2.0Moz plateau. SBC is 0.5% of revenue (Australian market, small); house/street band is narrow, not collapsed. Price is a regular-session print, not after-hours. Buybacks: A$128.9m actually spent in FY26 (financing activities), A$500m program remaining A$371m.

bear.narrative: The 2023-26 gold run reverses the way 2011-15 did: realised price falls to A$3,600/oz by FY30 (about the FY25 realised level, ~US$2,500) and drifts 2%/yr. KCGM's 27Mtpa ramp is slow and lower-grade for longer (bottom of FY27 guidance, ~750koz steady state), Hemi FID slips and the project is deferred/scoped down, so group output plateaus ~2.0Moz. Unit cash costs stay near the FY27 guided level because NST is not a first-quartile producer and cannot cut its way to FY26 margins; the CEO transition and Elliott board fight distract execution. EBITDA margin compresses to ~33-35%, capex is cut to sustaining-plus-development, and the terminal owner-FCF is thin.

base.narrative: FY27 inside guidance (1,560koz, AISC ~A$3,250 mid) at a realised price near the H2 FY26 exit rate; KCGM ramps to ~900kozpa by FY29-30 on the 27Mtpa mill; Hemi FID late FY27, first gold FY30, group ~2.4Moz by FY34 (company target 2.5Moz by FY29 haircut for the FY25/FY26 misses). Gold reverts to a A$4,400 mid-cycle by FY30. Unit cash costs improve with KCGM scale then inflate ~2.5%/yr; EBITDA margin settles at 44-45% (FY22-24 range 43-51%). Capex intensity falls from 35% (KCGM completion + Hemi build + Fimiston South) to 18% sustaining-plus-development.

bull.narrative: Gold holds a structurally higher plateau (A$5,200-5,700/oz, still below the Sep-2026 spot-equivalent) on sustained central-bank demand; KCGM hits the top of FY27 guidance and 900koz steady state by FY29; Hemi delivers the company's 2.5Mozpa by FY29-31; scale drives unit cash costs down to ~A$2,250/oz before inflating. The Elliott-driven board refresh improves capital discipline rather than disrupting execution. EBITDA margins hold ~55-58%, roughly FY25-26 levels.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30%: the valuation year is a gold-price peak, NST is above-peer on AISC so margin compression in a pullback is more severe than for first-quartile producers, and the growth plan has already missed once (the 2Moz FY26 target) while the CEO seat is turning over under an activist campaign. Bull cut to 25% because it needs two independent things to hold at once, a spot-like gold price for a decade AND on-time delivery of both KCGM and Hemi. Base 45%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
